newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says 5 consortia bid on Merida III gas duct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says 5 consortia bid on Merida III gas duct.

text.p: The Mexican government said Tuesday that five consortia from the United States, Canada, Japan and Mexico had made bids to build and operate a gas pipeline to fuel the planned Merida III power plant in the Yucatan peninsula.

It named the companies and consortia as Gasoductos Enron de Yucatan; Nova Corporation in conjunction with The Williams Companies Inc and Perez Companc International Limited; Gutsa Construcciones with Merida Pipeline Company Limited and Transcanada Pipelines Limited ; Bufete Industrial Construcciones with Shell Oil Co and Mitsui & Co Ltd ; and Epic Yucatan with Gas del Sur, Constructora ICA and Snam Spa.

The pipeline, which will require an investment of about $350 million, will run for more than 500 km from Ciudad Pemex in Tabasco state to the Yucatan and carry about 10.4 million cubic feet per day of natural gas.

All five consortia had already passed a technical evaluation of their bids and Mexican officials unsealed their economic bids Tuesday. The winner would be announced within 30 days, the Federal Electricity Commission said in a statement.
The pipeline will also feed other power plants in the Yucatan region once they have been converted to natural gas, it said.
Mexico is seeking some $800 million in private investment in total to build the pipeline and the planned Merida III power plant as part of a program to expand its electricity generating capacity.
